notes.title: How is the full version of Strategic Mind: The Pacific planned to differ from the EA version?
notes.content:
We want to keep you informed about how our work progresses. So, here is the table representing the comparison of our expectations for the Early access version (at launch, April 30) and the Full release version of the game.

[table]
    [tr]
        [th][b]Features[/b][/th]
        [th][b]Early access (April 30)[/b][/th]
        [th][b]Full release[/b][/th]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [th]Core content[/th]
        [th]First 3 operations of the USA campaign[/th]
        [th]2 full campaigns: the USA and the Empire of Japan[/th]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [th]Estimated playtime[/th]
        [th]10 hours[/th]
        [th]60+ hours[/th]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [th]Cutscenes[/th]
        [th]None (work in progress)[/th]
        [th]Before and after each operation[/th]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [th]Voice acting[/th]
        [th]None (only text)[/th]
        [th]Full [/th]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [th]Rewards[/th]
        [th]Full (for 3 operations)[/th]
        [th]Full[/th]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [th]Units[/th]
        [th]Full (for 3 operations)[/th]
        [th]Full[/th]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [th]Units progression[/th]
        [th]Full (for 3 operations)[/th]
        [th]Full[/th]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [th]Units skills[/th]
        [th]90% ready[/th]
        [th]100% ready[/th]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [th]HQ skills [/th]
        [th]50% ready[/th]
        [th]100% ready[/th]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [th]Equipment[/th]
        [th]50% ready[/th]
        [th]100% ready[/th]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [th]Icons[/th]
        [th]50% ready[/th]
        [th]100% ready[/th]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [th]Core mechanics[/th]
        [th]100% ready (some rework and polishing might be needed)[/th]
        [th]100% ready and polished[/th]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [th]Day/night and rain[/th]
        [th]100% ready[/th]
        [th]100% ready[/th]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [th]Heroes[/th]
        [th]None (at launch)[/th]
        [th]All[/th]
    [/tr]
[/table]

Let us go over the main points and provide you with more detail.

As many of you could have guessed, [b]cutscenes [/b]require lots of effort. We have already done the script and other preliminary work, however, there are still much to do in this regard. So we do not expect them to be ready before the full release.

The similar situation exists regarding the [b]voice acting[/b]. We have to finalise all the lines before making and implementing voice acting.

All units and [b]rewards [/b]for Early access are already in the game. As well as most of the skills.

[b]HQ skills[/b], equipment and icons are work in progress.

[b]Core mechanics[/b] are ready, but require additional testing and polishing both before and after the beginning of Early access stage.
Day/night and rain features are now being tested.

We plan to add [b]heroes [/b]after the beginning of Early access as the work progresses and we deal with more crucial elements of the game.

We hope that this portion of content will help you understand what to expect from the Full version of the game (apart from cutscenes). And, on the other hand, your feedback would help us make the Full version even better.

We want our development process to be as transparent as possible without spoiling too much of the actual game. We want you to be informed about our work, but at the same time keep some surprises in store for the time when you will finally be able to launch the game.

notes.title: Japanese carrier-based aircraft in Strategic Mind: The Pacific
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34062974/32454cc114d7119965e24d1da8355c70c5a48105.jpg[/img]Last week we have told you about the USA carrier-based aviation. Today, it is the Empire of Japan`s turn.

Japanese carrier-based fighters(1) are famous Mitsubishi A6M Type 0 “Zero” aircraft, which showed an outstanding performance in the early years of the war.

Carrier-based dive-bombers(3) are D3A and D4Y. They were carrying only 250 and 500 kg of bombs respectively and thus could not carry an 800 kg Type 91 aerial torpedo. (While the USA dive-bomber SB2C was able to carry 900 kg Mark 13 aerial  torpedoes, even though not as effectively as torpedo bombers). 

SB2C models are the only carrier-based dive-bombers in the game, eligible to carry torpedoes, even though it hinders their fighting capabilities. 
 
Carrier-based torpedo bombers(2) are Nakajima B5N and B6N models. Executing successful torpedo attacks upon enemy naval forces is a crucial part of the game and requires not only torpedo bombers but also fighters to protect them and oftentimes dive-bombers to organise a combined attack using both bombs and torpedoes.

notes.title: Carrier ships in Strategic Mind: The Pacific
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34062974/c977620083f508a71190cc3c20327f246971b999.gif[/img]As you may already know Strategic Mind: The Pacific will have mobile floating airfields - [b]carrier ships[/b]. 

They can take up to [b]5 aircraft units[/b] on board depending on their class. Thus carriers have by far the biggest reach: they [b]can attack as far as their planes could fly[/b] and return safely. 

Keeping your carriers at a safe distance to continue attacking from afar, and in turn, locating the positions of the enemy carriers is the [b]key to winning major naval battles[/b]. 

Carriers are also a valuable asset during landing operations: [b]providing air support to your land troops [/b]is the task of great importance. 

Carriers are both deadly and vulnerable, which makes them a top priority target for the enemy forces. [b]Be warned that the enemy will try to locate[/b] and destroy your carrier ships by any means. 

Thus you should take great care in safeguarding them with your escort ships and other naval forces. Carriers were a novelty at the time and not all of naval officers realised the full extent of their power. 

You will have a chance[b] to unleash the full potential of carrier forces upon your enemy [/b]and prove your strategic superiority.

notes.title: Terrain types in Strategic Mind: The Pacific
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34062974/70b6afe0e314d7be68426c12e80b816ba7aaf395.jpg[/img]Most of the time your fleet would be in the Ocean waging naval and aerial battles. However, numerous landing operations like [b]the Battle of Iwo Jima[/b] and the [b]Battle of Okinawa [/b]will require your troops to advance through land. The best place to land is [b]Clear [/b]terrain. 

However, oftentimes you would have to land in the [b]Shallows [/b]- which hinders your advance and makes your troops an easy target. 

Upon overtaking coastal area you will proceed to fight in [b]Forest [/b]terrain which provides good hiding places as well as better defensive capabilities but hinders your onslaught. 

[b]Mountains [/b]are the best place to build an impenetrable defence. [b]Rough [/b]terrain is difficult both to attack and to move into.

It is best to avoid moving your troops through [b]Swamp [/b]and [b]Fields[/b], especially your wheeled units. There are following types of land units movement in the game: on foot, wheeled, half-tracked, tracked, towed etc. It is important to understand the pros and cons of each type and to provide them with sound tactical command. 

[b]Small rivers[/b] run between hexes and make attacking across them an unfavourable endeavour, unless your troops have a clear advantage. A [b]bridge [/b]would allow your troop to cross the river without reducing the tempo of your advance.

In future updates we will provide you with more info on [b]City [/b]hexes and infrastructure as well as other aspects of the game.

notes.title: Strategic Mind: the Pacific free keys from Santa
notes.content:
As the New Year approaches our development team asked Santa to provide gifts for our upcoming game Strategic Mind: the Pacific to the most active and helpful Panzer Strategy community members. After long and deliberate investigation of Panzer Strategy community hub Santa has made up his mind and decided whom to present with keys for the upcoming Strategic Mind: the Pacific game (as soon as it hits Early access). 

Those of you who have contributed to our community hub in a variety of ways: a) helped us by accurately and promptly reporting bugs and sending us save files or other info necessary to fix them; b) helped us by sharing your view of the game and providing constructive criticism and lots of valuable feedback; c)  helped our community on Steam by sharing your knowledge with others and supporting them in learning our far-from-straightforward game. d) other activities which Santa has noticed and approved of; … and any combination of the above. 

There is no guaranteed recipe to be on Santa`s list - he just decided that he would like to commend you guys for playing our game and actively sharing your experience. Santa hopes that those who did not make it into the list will forgive him and offer him an opportunity to give them a gift next time.

Here is Santa`s list: Kiane, donee, stevenmiller353, Stonedog, bcnkor, Tim, Blackhawk, Skeptomatik, FUUKamikazeFUU, Naughty Mouse, wh056, SalzStange, Grondel the 10/10, Ninjachicken, Praetorian, True_Blue and others. 

Santa hopes you will enjoy his New Year gift, though he is very busy and will not be able to deliver it to you before the end of February.

notes.title: Untitled
How to get heroes in Panzer Strategy?
notes.content:
[b]Each hero has a specific requirement to obtain. [/b]

Here is the list:
[b]Hans-Ulrich Rudel[/b]
You have to deal 70+ damage* with your tactical bomber to land or naval enemy units and use Air recon HQ skill 10+ times. 
[b]Can serve in: [/b]tactical bomber.

[b]Kurt Knispel[/b]
You have to deal 70+ damage* with your tank to the enemy tanks, recon units, anti-tanks (only damage to these types of units counts).
[b]Can serve in:[/b] tank. 

[b]Michael Wittmann[/b]
You have to deal 50+ damage* with your tank or self-propelled anti-tank to the enemy tanks, recon units, anti-tanks (only damage to these types of units counts).
[b]Can serve in: [/b]tank, self-propelled anti-tank. 

[b]Rudolf Witzig[/b]
You have to deal 60+ damage* with your infantry unit to the enemy forts and coastal batteries (only damage to these types of units counts).
[b]Can serve in:[/b] infantry.

[b]Fritz Christen[/b]
You have to deal 20+ damage* with your anti-tank unit to enemy units(any) while this unit (your anti-tank) has 4 or less strength (In the next update we plan to increase it to “6 or less strength”).
[b]Can serve in: [/b]anti-tank.

*The damage has to be done with a single unit across any number of missions. Each of your units of corresponding type has its own counter, so they all work towards the final goal independently. However, once the first unit reaches the requirement, you gain a hero and all counters for this hero are frozen.

notes.title: Strategic Mind: The Pacific
notes.content:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A-NHBOzGk3E
Hello everyone,
 
We want to keep you informed about what is going on with the development of the Panzer Strategy game and everything related to it.

When our Panzer Strategy game came out many of our players voiced an opinion that the name of the game poorly reflected the overall scope and complexity of the game which has much more to it than just tank battles: strategic development of your army, naval warfare, various types of aviation - you name it. We agree with the public opinion on that matter. 

However, we decided against changing the name of Panzer Strategy as it would cause unnecessary confusion. Nonetheless, we adhere to your idea and would like to inform you that our future games will be out under the “Strategic Mind” title.
 
We are happy to announce our new project Strategic Mind: the Pacific - the successor of Panzer Strategy with brand new features.

There is the link to the game page where you can learn more about the new game and its features as the information gradually becomes available.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/991810/Strategic_Mind_The_Pacific 

Do not fret, however, as we will not abandon the support and future improvement of the Panzer Strategy game: moreover we released a few patches recently addressing many issues and implementing new features and we have already planned a lot of new stuff we want to implement in the upcoming updates as our work progresses. 

Both projects are being processed simultaneously and we believe that making Panzer Strategy a better game will also help us improve the quality of the upcoming Strategic Mind: the Pacific.

We hope that you will keep supporting us in our undertakings as you are the sole reason for us to keep doing what we are doing.

notes.title: Patch v1.20 of 20 November 2018
notes.content:
[h1]Major changes[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]New saving system[/b]. (Now all saves are separate files (instead of one big file with info about all saves) and are stored in the following default folder on your PC C:\Users\%Username%\AppData\Local\StarniGames\PanzerStrategy. 
[/list]
Please note that “AppData” is a hidden folder. So, now you can copy, delete etc individual saves or any number of them as it suits you. Back up your saves and so on (now you can safely uninstall the game without losing save files). 

This change, however, came at a cost. We managed to preserve your saves made during the strategic phase of the game (between missions), but unfortunately the saves made during any given mission before this patch are now unavailable. 

Also note that all land vehicles (ground transport) attached to units were sold and their cost in prestige added to your prestige, so you can buy them back. We are sorry to disrupt your gameplay and hope that availability of strategic phase saves will curb the damage. We were anxious to make this step as we did not want to disappoint our players. However, we understood that there were no other way to move forward without this painful step. 

This new system is a huge step toward adopting steam cloud saves as well as better steam integration and other juicy stuff in future. It also helped us fix some of the existing issues and prevent some future problems before they came.

We hope that you will forgive us this inconvenience for the sake of unhindered future development of the game.
[list]
[*][b]Added “Continue” button[/b] in main menu PSB-2209 
[*][b]Added quick save/quick load[/b] (F5/F8) PSB-2116
[*][b]Command Points gain per turn[/b] now depends on the number of deployed core units. (Instead of core units) So, now you can omit deploying part of your army in certain missions to ensure more Command points income per turn.  PSB-2367
[*][b]Fixed not playing cutscene[/b] after Operation Sea Lion. PSB-2247
[*][b]Major rework of damage distribution when attacking ships[/b].[/list]
Now damage is distributed more evenly among all ship parts and hull. So, you basically need to wipe out all ship modules before you can sink a ship|(in most cases), unless you use torpedoes (which always damage only hull). 

Torpedoes now do not apply statistic reduction, and reduce movement of the ship by 1. We are eager to let you try out the new damage distribution system, as we think it provides major increase in tactical thinking required for successful naval battles and reduces their randomness by huge margin. PSB-2345
[list]
[*][b]Vulnerability mechanic has been removed[/b] from the game. (In previous versions ship`s AA guns, depth charges and torpedo tubes received x2 damage.)
[*][b]Ships and submarines now can resupply[/b] their ammo and fuel at seaports. (You have to move them within 1 hexagon of a seaport.) PSB-2035
[*][b]Fixed capital ships BuildIn skill "Barrage fire"[/b].  Now it attacks (only) once with one of its secondary guns.) PSB-2309
[*][b]Added line of fire for artillery. [/b]All artillery units: ship guns, land artillery and coastal batteries now cannot attack enemy units obstructed by mountain (and unpassable mountain) terrain. New label “No line of fire” indicates that you cannot fire at that target from current position due to terrain factor. PSB-2288
[*][b]Air units (fighters and bombers) can now move[/b] 1 hex after being stopped mid air with overwatch ability (eg. AA overwatch fire).  PSB-2258, PSB-2293
[*][b]Fighters now can move 1 hex[/b] after attacking land units. (Same as bombers. Note that it does not allow them to move after attacking air targets) PSB-2280
[*][b]Fixed coastal artillery. [/b]Now it works similar to Forts. PSB-2065 Coastal artillery now has range 3 (in its zone of fire). Beware! PSB-2297
[*][b]Increased defense bonus for units[/b] if the enemy has no full information about the unit. If the unit is unknown (no unit type info, shown by ? on the map) defense increased by 4 (it was 2).  If the unit is spotted (its type is known, shown by ?? in place of unit strength) defense increased by 2 (it was 1) PSB-2261
[*][b]Added info (flying label) [/b]"Unidentified target: damage reduced" when firing at unidentified (unknown or spotted, see above)) unit.  PSB-2243
[*] Minimum entrenchment level for CloseDefence to apply increased from 3 to 4. (It means infantry has to be better entrenched to use CloseDefence parameter of armored units in combat. Makes armored units stronger vs infantry in certain situations.) PSB-2263
[*] Bombers now can return fire even if they have no ammo left. (It is the only type of units in the game which does not use its ammo for return fire, and uses it only for attacks.) PSB-1957
[*] Fixed support mechanics to check not only units attack value but also their current strength when choosing the most powerful unit to provide support. 
[/list]
When two or more units are eligible for support at the same time) Now ships AA guns would not support if there is fighter to provide support. (Ship`s AA has more air attack then fighter, but only 2 strength. So it would support only if there is a fighter with 2-3 hp contesting right to support) Same applies for artillery etc. PSB-2254
[list]
[*] [b]You can now see Build In Skills[/b] (skills which are same for all units of that class) (Do not confuse it with Level Up Skills which are chosen during level ups - those are seen only if you have full info about the enemy unit( as before)) of an enemy unit if it is spotted (unknown strength), earlier it was shown only if you have full information about unit. PSB-2211
[*] [b]Rebalanced activation costs of HQ skills[/b]: Aviation recon and Blitzkrieg +1 activation cost, Tank onslaught - unchanged, Frontline artillery -1 activation cost, Strategic bombing -1 activation cost.
[*] [b]Added info (flying label) "Initiative won"[/b] when unit wins initiative contest. (It is always attacking unit. If it wins initiative, it still attacks second (unless it has First Strike ability) but gains +4 to defence for the time of enemy counter attack.  PSB-2256
[*] [b]Some positive[/b] (eg. unit is entrenched; or it is near HQ) [b]and negative [/b](eg. unit is in the river; or it was already attacked this turn)[b] effects on units are now also displayed[/b] via a green or red icon (tick) on the unit. (You still can see all the effects in unit parameters window) The “ticks” stuck up to 3 and if the number of effects is higher then there is number under the “tick” going up. (Ticks usually show number of effects, the only exceptions are entrenchment and previous attacks where each level of entrenchment or each attack adds a separate “tick”. PSB-2289, PSB-2300, PSB-2302, PSB-2328, PSB-2337
[*] [b]Some hot keys effects are now shown[/b] via text on the screen. PSB-1589
[*] [b]Added symbol (<<) "Upgrade available"[/b] during the strategic screen. It is shown when there are new models available in this type of units after the last mission.  PSB-2269
[/list]
[h1]Other fixes and improvements[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Fixed: Air units no longer gain bonuses[/b] (+4 to defence, +1 camouflage) when they are in a hex with building (eg. in Dunkirk or Stalingrade map) as if it was an infantry occupying that building.
[*] [b]Bombers now do not counterattack with bombing[/b] if the enemy ship is attacking them with AA gun from underneath (same hex, range 0). PSB-2375
[*] [b]Changed flying labels for damage to various ship parts[/b]. Now they reflect the type of part (eg. Anti-Aircraft Gun, Secondary Gun, Torpedo Tube) instead of exact part name (eg. 2 x 37 mm 50 Mle, 8 x 105 mm SKC/33, 4 x G7a 533 mm) Also, now damage to the ship hull is marked as “-x Hull” instead of plain “-x”. If not a single ship part took damage from an attack, “0” is shown.
[*] [b]Fixed torpedo tube with 0 hp being able to attack[/b] (for 0 damage) and put a -1 penalty for previous attack on the enemy. (Now it cannot be used) PSB-2291
[*] [b]Fixed torpedo tubes being able to shoot[/b] at the enemy ship through 1 hex of land PSB-2362
[*] [b]Torpedo tubes now cannot shoot at the enemy ship through a hex[/b] with another friendly or enemy ship. PSB-2377
[*] [b]Fixed train (and some other auxiliary units) having 0 spotting range[/b]. PSB-2343
[*] [b]Now units do not lose entrenchment levels if they attack without moving[/b] into another hex. (So you can now attack units next to the entrenched unit without losing its entrenchment) PSB-2356
[*] [b]Now after deploying one unit, next unit on the list is auto selected[/b]. (Earlier the first unit on the list was auto selected) PSB-2301
[*] [b]Fixed “Commissar” skill [/b]having no description. PSB-2222
[*] [b]Fixed “Poorly trained” skill[/b] having no description. PSB-2223
[*] [b]Fixed LinkedFight bug[/b] when you could use this ability before movement and then move.(Which is illegal due to LinkedFight description) PSB-2251
[*] [b]Fixed infantry on board a train being able to entrench[/b]. PSB-2339
[*] [b]In Battle for Atlantic mission fixed bug[/b] with rain effects lasting long after the rain has finished. PSB-2364
[*] [b]Fixed paratroopers in the air[/b] (transportation) gaining full fuel after save/load. PSB-2084
[*] [b]Fixed incorrect display of fuel [/b](shown as full) and movement left (shown as max) of units in transportation mode after save/load. PSB-2195
[*] [b]Fixed icon for paratroopers disembarking from a ship[/b] (it was shown as a parachute as if they were disembarking from plane) PSB-2143
[*] [b]Fixed message when trying to disembark at seaport[/b] with all eligible hexes being already occupied. (It was saying you have to disembark at seaport) PSB-2144
[*] [b]Fixed message when trying to disembark at enemy controlled seaport[/b]. It was saying you have to disembark at seaport. PSB-2148
[*] [b]Fixed all AI embarked landing forces in Norway[/b] on “Marshall” difficulty level having 10 strength instead of 12. PSB-2366
[*] [b]Added "Click for detailed info"[/b] when you mouse hover over units parameters. PSB-2257
[*] [b]Fixed incorrect info[/b] “You do not have enough HQ points to learn a new HQ skill” after you already learned all levels of that skill. PSB-2182
[*] [b]Fixed minor bug with leveling up units skills[/b] PSB-2181
[*] [b]Fixed reinforcement of units cost 0 prestige[/b] while unit is on the train.  PSB-2121
[*] [b]Fixed some issues with support firing range for certain units[/b]. PSB-2086
[*] [b]If you have AirRecon or AirStrike skill selected[/b] and choose where on the map to apply it, you now can cancel it by left clicking any allied unit. PSB-2152
[*] [b]Double clicking on the unit in “Reserve” tab will now center the camera[/b] on the nearest deploy hex. PSB-2281
[*] [b]Added info “Available between missions[/b]” for icons of increase/decrease unit strength”(-/+) and “disband” on units during the mission. PSB-2017
[*] [b]Added infohints for icons of increase/decrease unit strength[/b]”(-/+) and “disband” on units during the strategic screen and deploy phase. PSB-2017
[*] [b]Added visual effect for new secondary objective[/b] when you get it during the mission. PSB-2190
[*] [b]Fixed Rommel “Aggressive” skill tooltip [/b]description (changed “+2 initiative from HQ” to “Erwin Rommel: gain +2 initiative”) not to be misleading. 
[*] [b]Fixed water animation shown in incorrect hexes[/b] when moving ships. PSB-2162
[*] [b]Fixed some problems with water animation[/b]. PSB-1860
[*] [b]Fixed unit with less than 0 hp (took more damage than had hp) lingering too long[/b] before disappearing if you skip animation. PSB-2298
[*] [b]Fixed some city hexes on Dunkirk map [/b]not having city name on them. PSB-2179
[*] [b]Fixed various text inaccuracies [/b]in English and Russian versions of the game.
[*] [b]Fixed flying label for ships BarrageFire skill activation[/b] displaying incorrect text in Russian localisation. PSB-2213

* This list does not include some of the issues solved and inaccuracies fixed.

Unternehmen Seelöwe
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/z82UGGS.png[/img]
Am 16. Juli 1940 erließ Hitler die Führerrichtlinie Nr. 16, welche die Vorbereitungen für eine Landung in Großbritannien in Gang setzte.
 
Er hatte den Beschluß mit folgenden Worten vorgetragen: "Da England trotz seiner hoffnungslosen militärischen Lage immer noch keine Bereitschaft zur Verständigung zeigt, habe ich beschlossen, eine Landungsoperation gegen sie vorzubereiten und gegebenenfalls durchzuführen. Ziel dieser Operation ist es, das englische Mutterland als Basis zu eliminieren, von dem aus der Krieg gegen Deutschland fortgesetzt werden kann, und, wenn nötig, das Land vollständig zu besetzen."
 
Der Codename für die Invasion war "Seelöwe". Als Vorbedingung nannte er die Erreichung der Luft- und Marineüberlegenheit über dem Ärmelkanal und die sehr wichtigen Landeplätze der britischen Airforce. Die deutschen Streitkräfte erreichten zu keinem Zeitpunkt die nötige Überlegenheit und sowohl das deutsche Oberkommando als auch Hitler selbst hatten ernsthafte Zweifel an den Erfolgsaussichten.
 
Eine große Anzahl von Lastkähnen war an der Kanalküste versammelt, aber mit zunehmenden Verlusten der Luftwaffe verschob Hitler die Operation Seelöwe am 17. September 1940 auf unbestimmte Zeit und hat sie nie fortgesetzt.
 
Zwar wurde die Operation Seelöwe 1940 nicht gestartet. Aber in Panzer Strategie können Sie jedoch im Falle eines brillanten Sieges in der Schlacht um England Großbritannien angreifen. Sie müssen La Manche überqueren und eine Landung im Südosten von Großbritannien starten. Das nächste Ziel ist es, die britischen Truppen in den Norden zu drängen und London zu erobern.

notes.title: July 16 in WWII - Hitler issued Operation Sea Lion
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/z82UGGS.png[/img]
On July 16, 1940 Hitler issued Fuhrer Directive No. 16, setting in motion preparations for a landing in Britain. 

He prefaced the order by stating: "As England, in spite of her hopeless military situation, still shows no signs of willingness to come to terms, I have decided to prepare, and if necessary to carry out, a landing operation against her. The aim of this operation is to eliminate the English Motherland as a base from which the war against Germany can be continued, and, if necessary, to occupy the country completely." 

The code name for the invasion was Seelowe, "Sea Lion". As a precondition, he specified the achievement of both air and naval superiority over the English Channel and the proposed landing sites, but the German forces did not achieve either at any point during the war, and both the German High Command and Hitler himself had serious doubts about the prospects for success. 

A large number of barges were gathered together on the Channel coast, but, with air losses increasing, Hitler postponed Sea Lion indefinitely on September 17, 1940 and it was never put into action.

The Operation Sea Lion did not start in 1940. However in Panzer Strategy you will be able to attack Britain in case of brilliant victory in the Battle of Britain. You’ll have to cross La Manche and launch a landing operation on the South-East of Great Britain. The next objective is to push the British forces to the north and to conquer London.

notes.title: July 10 in World War II - the Battle of Britain begins
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/9tog6vD.jpg[/img]
On July 10 1940, the Battle of Britain begins with Luftwaffe raids on channel shipping. The Battle of Britain takes its name from a speech by Winston Churchill to the House of Commons: "What General Weygand has called The Battle of France is over. The Battle of Britain is about to begin."

The Germans had rapidly overwhelmed France and the Low Countries, leaving Britain to face the threat of invasion by sea. The German high command knew the difficulties of a seaborne attack and its impracticality while the Royal Navy controlled the English Channel and the North Sea.

The primary objective of the German forces was to compel Britain to agree to a negotiated peace settlement. In July 1940 the air and sea blockade began, with the Luftwaffe mainly targeting coastal-shipping convoys, ports and shipping centers.

As the battle progressed, the Luftwaffe also targeted factories involved in aircraft production and strategic infrastructure. Eventually, the Germans began terror bombing on areas of political significance and on civilians.
The Battle of Britain was the first major military campaign fought entirely by air forces.

In 1940 The Royal Air Force defended the UK against large-scale attacks by Luftwaffe. The German failure to destroy Britain's air defenses was the first major defeat of Nazi Germany in WWII.

In Panzer Strategy we try to simulate the tide of this campaign. For the “Battle of Britain” scenario we’ve made lots of unique 3D models of WWII planes. The air battles are a very important part of Panzer Strategy mechanics, because often aircraft is the key to victory.

notes.title: July 6 in World War II - the Germans reached Voronezh
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/1wN6Hzu.jpg[/img]
On July 6 1942, General Hermann Hoth's forces swap aside the Soviet defence and reached the outskirts of Voronezh.  

First Battle of Voronezh fought in and around the strategically important city of Voronezh on the Don river, 450 km south of Moscow. It continued from June 24 to July 28 1942, as opening move of the German summer offensive in 1942.

The German attack had two objectives. One was to seed confusion about the ultimate goals of the overall campaign. 

The other purpose was to provide an easily defended front line along the river, providing a strong left flank that could be protected with relatively light forces.

Since July 7 Hoth continued to push forward. But then Soviet forces mounted a successful counterattack that tied up Hoth's forces.

The 3rd Motorized Division broke across the Don, but turned back. The Soviet command poured reserves into the city and a situation not unlike what would be seen at Stalingrad a few months later broke out, with the German troops clearing the city street by street with flamethrowers while tanks gave fire support.

The 2nd Motorized Division continued the battle until July 24, when the final Soviet forces to the west of the Don were defeated and the fighting ended.

Adolf Hitler later came to believe that these two days, when combined with other avoidable delays on the drive South, allowed Marshal Timoshenko to reinforce the forces in Stalingrad before the 4th Panzer Army could arrive to allow the taking of Stalingrad.

notes.title: July 5 in World War II - Operation Citadel
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/jIIJ1TV.jpg[/img]
On July 5 1943, the Operation Citadel started. It was a German offensive operation against Soviet forces in the Kursk salient that initiated the Battle of Kursk. 

The German offensive was countered by two Soviet counter-offensives. For the Germans, the battle was the final strategic offensive that they were able to launch on the Eastern Front. 

Kursk scenario map is the biggest in Panzer Strategy at the moment. The map is made with 3000 individual hexes. The feature of this scenario are the most intensive ground battles in the whole game. Also, both sides of the battle will have a large number of armored vehicles.

The Germans hoped to weaken the Soviet offensive potential by cutting off a large number of forces. The plan envisioned an envelopment by a pair of pincers breaking through the northern and southern flanks of the Kursk salient. 

The Germans delayed the offensive while they tried to build up their forces and waited for not only new weapons, like the new Panther tank but also larger numbers of Tigers. But the Soviet government had foreknowledge of the German intentions, provided in part by the British intelligence service. So the Soviets built a defense in depth designed to wear down the German armored spearhead. The defensive preparations included minefields, fortifications, artillery fire zones and anti-tank strong points.

For the first time, a major German offensive had been stopped before achieving a breakthrough. The Germans, despite using more technologically advanced armor than in previous years, were unable to break through the in-depth Soviet defenses and were caught off guard by the significant operational reserves of the Red Army. 

The Soviet victory was costly. The Red Army lost considerably more men and material than the German Army. However, the Soviet Union's larger industrial potential and pool of manpower allowed them to absorb and replenish these losses. After this operation, the Germans were lacking strategic reserves when western air power had started viciously devastating the Luftwaffe and penetrating into Italy.

notes.title: June 29 in World War II - Battle of Mersa Matruh
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/ei7eFXh.jpg[/img]
On June 29 1942, the 90th Light Division and Italian Littorio Armored Division encircled Mersa Matruh. The Battle of Mersa Matruh was fought following the defeat of the Eighth Army at the Battle of Gazala. 

Following the victory at Tobruk Rommel pressed on the heels of the retreating Eighth Army. His intention was to bring the Eighth Army to battle and defeat it before the British had the chance to bring up fresh units and reform behind a defensive line.

In the event, he was able to cut off the line of retreat of X Corps and the XIII Corps, but his forces were too weak to stop them from breaking out. 

The Mersa Matruh positions had been under heavy artillery fire from the Brescia and Trento Divisions, which along with the German 90th Light Division represented the main force invested in the stronghold.

After some time of infantry fighting and failed breakout attempts, the stronghold sought to capitulate. The fortress port of Mersa Matruh and 6,000 prisoners fell into Rommel's hands there, along with plenty of supplies and equipment, but the main goal of destroying the Eighth Army escaped him.

notes.title: June 28 in World War II – Case Blau
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/Z5NJlec.jpg[/img]
On June 28 1942 the German Armed Forces started a strategic summer offensive in southern Russia codenamed Case Blau. The operation was a continuation of the previous year's Operation Barbarossa, intended to knock the Soviet Union out of the war. 

Supported by 2,035 Luftwaffe aircrafts and 1,934 tanks and assault guns, the 1,370,287-man Army Group South attacked on June 28, advancing 48 kilometers on the first day and easily brushing aside the 1,715,000 Red Army troops opposition, who falsely expected a German offensive on Moscow even after Blau commenced. 

The Soviet collapse in the south allowed the Germans to capture the western part of Voronezh on July 6 and reach and cross the Don river near Stalingrad on July 26. 

The 6th Army reached the outskirts of Stalingrad. Much of the city was quickly turned to rubble, although some factories continued production while workers joined in the fighting. The Stalingrad Tractor Factory continued to turn out T-34 tanks literally until German troops burst into the plant.

Fighting within the ruined city was fierce and desperate. We could not skip the battle that is often regarded as the single largest and bloodiest battle in the history of warfare. 

Panzer Strategy Battle of Stalingrad game scenario includes such features as close quarters combat, Soviet plants supplying ammo and vehicles and a lot of snipers in the Soviet army including Vasily Zaytsev.

Due to the initial success of the German summer offensive in 1942, Hitler and the German commanders became more ambitious, putting great strain on the German army. Overextension reduced the capabilities of the German Army and its allies to defend this territory and the Soviets mounted a decisive offensive at Stalingrad, encircling the German army. 

The possibility that the Germans would continue to the south and east, and link up with Japanese forces in India, was of great concern to the Allies. But the Red Army defeated the Germans at Stalingrad, following Operations Uranus and Little Saturn. This defeat forced the Axis to retreat from the Caucasus.

notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/T45TNuc.png[/img]

notes.title: June 22 in World War II – Nazi Germany invaded the Soviet Union
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/X9qGorg.jpg[/img]
On June 22, 1941, the Axis started an invasion of the Soviet Union. It was codenamed Operation Barbarossa.

The Axis commenced the invasion of the Soviet Union with the bombing of major cities in Soviet-occupied Poland and an artillery barrage on Red Army defenses on the entire front. Air-raids were conducted as far as Kronstadt near Leningrad, Ismail in Bessarabia, and Sevastopol in the Crimea. 

Meanwhile, ground troops crossed the border. Roughly three million soldiers of the Wehrmacht, the largest invasion force in the history of warfare, went into action and faced slightly fewer Soviet troops at the border. Accompanying the German forces during the initial invasion were Finnish and Romanian units as well.

The initial momentum of the German ground and air attack completely destroyed the Soviet organizational command and control within the first few hours, paralyzing every level of command from the infantry platoon to the Soviet High Command in Moscow. 

The operation opened up the Eastern Front, in which more forces were committed than in any other theater of war in world history. The Eastern Front became the site of some of the largest battles, most horrific atrocities, and highest casualties for Soviet and Axis units alike, all of which influenced the course of both World War II and the subsequent history of the 20th century.

We have added several scenarios which took place on the Eastern Front. You will get into the Operation Barbarossa, Battle of Kiev, Siege of Leningrad, Operation Typhoon, Operation Fredericus, Fall Blau and Operation Citadel in the full version.

notes.title: June 21 in World War II – the Fall of Tobruk
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/6ZFlIU2.jpg[/img]
On June 21 Afrika Korps recaptured Tobruk with 35,000 men captured. The Afrika Korps demonstrated a superiority in tactics, combining tanks with anti-tank guns while on the offensive. Rommel acted rapidly on intelligence obtained from Allied radio traffic intercepts.

With the capture of Tobruk, the Axis gained a port near the Aegean–Crete route and a lot of British supplies. If the British would not stop the Germans later in Egypt, they would take the Suez Canal (forcing Britain to use supply lines twice as long, often targeted by U-boats) and potentially drive for the oilfields in the Middle East. 

Hitler rewarded Rommel with a promotion to the rank of field-marshal, the youngest German officer ever to achieve this rank. Rommel remarked he would have preferred Hitler had given him another panzer division instead.

Tobruk's loss was a grievous blow to British morale. Allied leaders expected Tobruk to be able to hold out for two months with the supplies in the fortress. Churchill wrote: "This was one of the heaviest blows I can recall during the war. Not only were its military effects grievous, but it had affected the reputation of the British armies".

notes.title: June 15 in World War II – Operation Battleaxe
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/B3fSRXP.jpg[/img]
On June 15 1941 Operation Battleaxe started. It was a British Army operation to clear eastern Cyrenaica of German and Italian forces and raise the Siege of Tobruk.

It was the first time during the war that a significant German force fought on the defensive, but the operation failed as British forces attacked strong defensive positions created by German general Erwin Rommel. The British lost over half of their tanks on the first day and only one of the three attacks succeeded.

The British achieved mixed results on the second day, being pushed back on their western flank and repulsing a big German counter-attack in the center. On the third day, the British narrowly avoided disaster by withdrawing just ahead of a German encircling movement. 

The British army lost 98 tanks, 33 fighters and 3 bombers compared to 50 disabled German tanks and 10 aircraft.
The Axis held the battlefield and recovered disabled vehicles. 

Churchill was displeased with the results of Operation Battleaxe. He had been expecting nothing less than complete success and had instead received news that the operation had failed and the tanks sent for it had been lost.

The Siege of Tobruk was lifted in December 1941 in the course of Operation Crusader. Nevertheless, Axis forces re-captured the port on 21 June 1942, after defeating the Eighth Army in the Battle of Gazala.

notes.title: June 14 in World War II – Paris fell
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/0cTIt5I.jpg[/img]
On June 14 1940 Paris fell. The French army organized a heavy defence of the capital, but the line was broken in several places.

In six weeks from May 10 German forces defeated Allies with mobile operations and conquered France, Belgium, Luxembourg and the Netherlands. German commanders met with French officials on June 18 with an intention to force the new French government to accept an armistice that amounted to surrender.

The Battle of France is the fourth Panzer Strategy game scenario. We have reproduced the German mobile operations against British, Belgian and French forces including the attack on the Maginot Line (fortifications along the border with Germany built by the French during the 1930s).

Also, we use heavy tank Char B1bis in this scenario. This French tank was a hard target for the Germans. It was a specialized break-through vehicle. 

Among the most powerfully armed and armored tanks of its day, Char B1bis was very effective in direct confrontations with German armor in 1940.

The occupation of the various French zones continued until November 1942, when the Allies began Operation Torch, the invasion of Western North Africa. On August 24 1944, Paris was liberated, and by September 1944 most of the country was in Allied hands.

Photo: https://www.iwm.org.uk

notes.title: June 8 in World War II – the sinking of HMS Glorious
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/6zwaHTE.jpg[/img]
On June 8, 1940, HMS Glorious was sunk by the German battleships Scharnhorst and Gneisenau while evacuating British aircraft from Norway.

HMS Glorious was the second of the three Courageous-class battlecruisers built for the Royal Navy during the World War I. Glorious was then rebuilt as an aircraft carrier during the late 1920s. It was recalled home in April 1940 to provide air cover for British forces landing in Norway. 

On the way through the Norwegian Sea the funnel smoke from Glorious and her two escorting destroyers, Acasta and Ardent, was spotted by Germans.

Glorious did not alter course or increase speed, no combat air patrol was launched, no aircraft was ready on the deck for a quick take-off.

Scharnhorst scored its first hit when one 28.3-centimetre shell hit the forward flight deck and burst into the upper hangar, starting a large fire. This hit destroyed two Swordfishes that were being prepared for flight and the hole in the flight deck prevented any other aircraft from taking off.

Glorious was hit again in the center engine room and this caused it to lose speed. The German ships closed to within 16,000 yards and continued firing. Glorious was sunk with over 1,200 lives lost. 

The Royal Navy knew nothing about the sinking until it was announced on German radio. The circumstances of the sinking were the subject of a debate in the House of Commons on January 28, 1999. The absence of normal airborne patrols over Glorious and its destroyers, in conditions of maximum visibility, were named as contributors to the sinkings.

Photo: https://www.historyinorbit.com

notes.title: June 3 in World War II – the Miracle of Dunkirk
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/9Q3haeb.jpg[/img]
June 3, 1940 was the last day of the Dunkirk evacuation.

The Battle of Dunkirk was a part of the larger Battle of France on the Western Front. By May 21 German forces had trapped the British Expeditionary Force, the remains of the Belgian forces, and three French field armies along the northern coast of France. The War Office made the decision to evacuate British forces on May 25 and began planning a withdrawal to Dunkirk, the closest port. 

The evacuation of Allied soldiers from the beaches and harbor of Dunkirk known as the Miracle of Dunkirk was code-named "Operation Dynamo".

Battle of Dunkirk will be the fifth scenario in Panzer Strategy and we will reproduce conditions of this dramatic battle. The scenario мap corresponds to the historical theatre of military operations during the Battle of Dunkirk. The troops, roads, cities and other objects are located at the historically accurate positions.

The German army was to halt for three days, which gave the Allies sufficient time to organize the Dunkirk evacuation and build a defensive line. Despite Luftwaffe attacks on British transport vessels, in the nine days, 338,226 men escaped aboard 861 vessels (243 were sunk during the operation). Luftwaffe lost about 135 aircrafts.

notes.title: June 1 in World War II – "Operation Mercury"
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/57ozObu.jpg[/img]
On June 1, 1940 commonwealth forces completed the withdrawal from Crete. The Battle of Crete (German: "Operation Mercury") began on the morning of May 20 when Germany began an airborne invasion of Crete. It was the first time when German [b]paratroopers were used en masse[/b]. 

We could not skip such a dramatic historical moment in the game. "Operation Mercury" is one of the late game scenarios where you’ll operate [b]only infantry units[/b]. 

It was the [b]first mainly airborne invasion in military history[/b]. So in the game, you have to use paratroopers to conquer Maleme airfield in western Crete enabling reinforcements to land.

Allied forces withdrew to the south coast. Over half were evacuated by the British Royal Navy; the remainder surrendered or joined the Cretan resistance. It was the first time German troops encountered mass resistance from a civilian population.

Although the conquest of Crete was considered a grand victory of the airborne corps, the German leadership focused on the heavy losses incurred. The German Air Ministry was shocked by the amount of transport aircraft lost. Due to the number of casualties and the belief that airborne forces no longer had the advantage of surprise, the German leadership preferred to employ paratroopers as ground troops. In contrast, the Allies were impressed by the potential of paratroopers and started to form airborne-assault and airfield-defense regiments.

The Battle of Crete is also known for the first time the Allies made significant use of intelligence from decrypted German messages from the Enigma machine.

notes.title: Panzer Strategy gets a massive update: a new scenario, updated graphics, performance improvements and a lot more
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/RPtBQqV.jpg[/img]
[b]On May 17 a massive update for Panzer Strategy rolls out[/b]!

It is bringing a whole new scenario ‘Operation Weserübung’, improved visuals, new units, a better AI, as well as numerous technical improvements. Panzer Strategy, currently on Steam Early Access, now features three full scenarios, latest Unreal Engine 4 graphics, and a lot more stable and polished gameplay with lots of content – moving the game closer to the final version quality. 

[b]The updated Panzer Strategy Early Access trailer[/b]:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ijdi-XGsqU0
[b]About ‘Operation Weserübung’ game scenario[/b]

The new scenario in the update is ‘Operation Weserübung’ – it is a Wehrmacht operation in Norway carried out between April 9 and June 8, 1940. The game’s version of the events takes place on the map with 1530 hexes. The key part of the scenario is naval warfare. You’ll be commanding warships, launching landings and managing coastal artillery – all packed with new gameplay mechanics. This makes ‘Operation Weserübung’ the most complex game scenario to date, with battles raging on land, at sea and in the air.

notes.title: May 12 in World War II – "Operation Fredericus"
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/O30nHvv.jpg[/img]
On May 12, 1942 Soviet forces under the command of Marshal Timoshenko launched an offensive against the German 6th Army from a salient established during the winter counter-offensive.

This [b]scenario in Panzer Strategy[/b] also combines the defense and counter-offensive. Like in 1942 the Soviet offensive is concentrated near Izium and the "Barvenkovo bulge" while he forces to the South near Voroshilovgrad (Lugansk) just hold the line. 

In 1942 the Soviet offensive was stopped on 15 May by a massive German campaign of airstrikes. Soviet command failed to accurately estimate the 6th Army's potential and overestimated their own newly raised forces and facilitated a German pincer attack. Hemmed into a narrow area, the 250,000-strong Soviet force was exterminated from all sides by German armored, artillery and machine gun firepower and after six days of encirclement the Soviet troops were either killed or taken prisoner.

In the [b]game scenario[/b] the key to success is a proper deployment of core-units. The units available at the start are insufficient to stop the offensive. So the German strategy is completely in your hands.

The battle turned to be an overwhelming German victory, with 280,000 Soviet casualties compared to 20,000 for the Germans and their allies. The German Army Group South pressed its advantage, encircling the Soviet 28th Army and pushing back the 38th and 9th Armies as preliminary operations to Case Blue, – a strategic summer offensive in southern Russia in 1942.

notes.title: May 10 in World War II
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/I4Py3Sa.jpg[/img]
On May 10, 1940 the Battle of France began. In six weeks from 10 May 1940, German forces defeated Allies with mobile operations and conquered France, Belgium, Luxembourg and the Netherlands. 

When British, Belgian and French forces were pushed back to the sea by a well-organized German operation, Great Britain evacuated the British Expeditionary Force (BEF) and several French divisions from Dunkirk in Operation Dynamo. These events are depicted in the forth and fifth Panzer Strategy scenarios. 

There Germans face Belgian and French forces, British Expeditionary Force, as well as Dutch and Luxembourg troops. The keystone of the ‘Fall Rot’ scenario is the Maginot Line, fortifications along the border with Germany. This fortification is historically accurate on the scenario map.
 
The French had built the Maginot Line During the 1930s. The line was intended to deter a German invasion across the Franch-German border and funnel an attack into Belgium. In 1940 Army Group C and Army Group A encircled and captured the French forces on the Maginot line. ‘Fall Rot’ was the second phase of the conquest of France. The remaining French divisions organized a heavy resistance, but were unable to overcome the German air superiority and armored mobility. 

In the game you have several strategic options. For instance, you can deploy all your troops in the South and assault the Maginot Line from the right flank. So you do not need to cross the channels to conquer Belgium. 

Also during this scenario you’ll encounter plenty of new units including the French heavy Char B1bis (pictured here). And of course, we couldn't skip the Battle of Dunkirk as a part of the Battle of France on the Western Front.

notes.title: Gameplay features in the new ‘Operation Weserübung’ scenario
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/TtDkmZp.jpg[/img]
Hey everyone!
 
The [b]big update[/b] is coming soon! Along with a more stable and polished game you’ll get a new scenario ‘Operation Weserübung’. As we’ve already mentioned, it takes place during the German invasion of Norway in 1940. The scenario features a map with 1530 hexes.
 
The first important change is that we’ve [b]improved the AI[/b]. It will act more strategically, attack with ships and launch troop landings. Moreover, we’ve added some scripted events. For example, after Germans are stranded on the coast of Norway, the British ships will arrive and their troops will land on the coast too.
 
There are a lot of [b]new units[/b] in this scenario including a coastal battery – a stationary unit for responding to attacks from the sea. It automatically engages enemy ships in its line of sight and can be captured via a ground attack.
 
The most complex part of the scenario are mechanics of [b]naval warfare[/b]. Ships have different systems aboard such as main guns, anti-aircraft guns, depth charges, torpedos, sonars and the propulsion system. All systems are destructible and have their own STR. For instance, if the propulsion system is damaged, the ship’s speed decreases. When an enemy attacks a ship, damage points are shared randomly between its systems. Armored systems such as the main battery lose 1 STR per 1 point of damage. Light or unarmored systems such as torpedo tubes or anti-air guns lose 2 STR per 1 point of damage.
 
When firing you can choose a weapon from a ship armament by left-clicking on a weapon icon on the right interface column. Otherwise a weapon will be picked automatically. 
 
Different types of [b]ships are well balanced[/b]. Destroyers are anti-battleship units. They attack a battleship with torpedos from a 2 hexagons range. The ‘Battleship secondary armament’ skill allows a battleship to fire at destroyers automatically when they come close enough for a torpedo attack. Also destroyers have a sonar which makes them ideal for hunting submarines – they are difficult to detect and deal massive damage to transports.
 
Thank you for your support and comments!

notes.title: April 21 – a turning point in the Battle of Greece
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/U0kWo8J.jpg[/img]
On this day in 1941 223,000 Greek soldiers of the Greek army in Albania surrendered, with their retreat cut off by the German advance.

Operation ‘Marita’ also known as the Battle of Greece was the invasion of Greece by Italian and German forces during World War II. It is the ninth scenario in Panzer Strategy – you’ll be commanding both German and Italian armies.

When the German invasion began on April 6, the main forces of the Greek Army were stationed on the border with Albania. The Italian troops attacked directly there and the Germans invaded from Bulgaria, creating a second front. In Panzer Strategy the Germans will also have several deploying zones to start the invasion. 

At the time Greece had already received some reinforcements from Britain, Australia and New Zealand, but that was it – no more help was sent afterwards. The Greek army found itself outnumbered against both Italian and German troops. The Metaxas defensive line didn’t receive adequate reinforcements and was quickly overrun by the Germans – the defensive line and the surrounding events will be featured in the scenario. 

The British, Australian and New Zealand forces were overwhelmed and were forced to retreat. The German Army reached Athens by April 27 capturing 7,000 British, Australian and New Zealand personnel and ending the battle with a decisive victory. The conquest of Greece was completed with the capture of Crete a month later – this mission will be featured in Panzer Strategy too.

Image credits: https://1.bp.blogspot.com/-u6jbRxowvg8/VzteE9ts59I/AAAAAAAAAz8/_a1Cs0X6oXsSnytwtiCn-78xNQNpekvwgCKgB/

notes.title: Find out more about the new ‘Operation Weserübung’ scenario
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/cRvExZO.jpg[/img]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/y2TGjh3.jpg[/img]
The new scenario in the upcoming Panzer Strategy update is ‘Operation Weserübung’. It is a Wehrmacht operation carried out between April 9 and June 8, 1940. The game’s version of the events takes place on the map with 1530 hexes.

German infantry and reconnaissance units start on the transport ships. They have to land on the western coast of Norway. Also Germans can begin an invasion with light land forces available on the first turn – with the support of aviation and naval artillery.
 
The operation involved large German ships: ‘Scharnhorst’ and ‘Gneisenau’ battleships, ‘Admiral Hipper’ cruiser, as well as Type VII submarines and German Type 1934 destroyers. They will face the Royal Navy at the sea. Also expeditionary forces transport ships approach the western coast of Norway in order to prevent the German occupation.

You will command the key battles of the Danish-Norwegian operation: the naval clash of ‘Scharnhorst’ and ‘Gneisenau’ with HMS Renown, the Royal Navy battle with German destroyers near Narvik and the German forces’ assault of Oslo from the sea.

This is the most complex operation of the first three scenarios:
[list]
[*]You have to command naval, air and ground forces at the same to secure the landing operation; 
[*]The AI acts strategically – in the same way as the Allies did;
[*]The are multiple ways to achieve victory.
[/list]

The update will be available in the coming weeks.

notes.title: On 23 August 1942 the 6th Army reached the outskirts of Stalingrad
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/Z5NJlec.jpg[/img]

The battle began with the heavy bombing of the city. Much of the city was quickly turned to rubble, although some [b]factories continued production[/b] while workers joined in the fighting. The Stalingrad Tractor Factory continued to turn out T-34 tanks literally until German troops burst into the plant.

Fighting within the ruined city was [b]fierce and desperate[/b]. Stalin's Order decreed that all commanders who ordered unauthorized retreat would be subject to a military tribunal.

The following scenario features are based on these facts: [b]close quarters combat[/b] and [b]Soviet plants supplying ammo and vehicles[/b].

notes.title: Battle of Moscow is one of Panzer Strategy future scenarios
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/rDkHV2c.jpg[/img]
Operation Barbarossa called for the capture of Moscow within [b]four months[/b]. 

The Soviet Union did everything to prevent it. The Soviet forces conducted a strategic defense by constructing [b]three defensive belts[/b]. 

Moscow itself was also [b]fortified[/b]. 250,000 women and teenagers worked building trenches and anti-tank moats around Moscow, moving almost three million m3 of earth with no mechanical help. 

The Luftwaffe launched large-scale air raids on the city but those raids caused only limited damage because of [b]extensive anti-aircraft defenses[/b] and effective civilian fire brigades.

And the last but not the least, the European Winter of 1941-1942 was [b]the coldest of the twentieth century[/b]. The lowest December temperature reached –30 °C. The German troops were freezing with no winter clothing, using equipment that was not designed for such low temperatures. The Soviet troops were better prepared for this.

notes.title: Battle of Kursk
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/Vn9OZOi.jpg[/img]
It was a WWII engagement between German and Soviet forces near Kursk. The battle was the final strategic offensive that the Germans were able to launch on the Eastern Front. 

[b]For the first time, a major German offensive had been stopped[/b] before achieving a breakthrough. The Germans, despite using more technologically advanced armor than in previous years, were unable to break through the in-depth Soviet defenses and were caught off guard by the significant operational reserves of the Red Army. 

The Soviet [b]victory, however, was costly[/b], with the Red Army losing considerably more men and material than the German Army. However, the Soviet Union's larger industrial potential and pool of manpower allowed them to absorb and replenish these losses.

Kursk map is [b]the biggest in Panzer Strategy[/b] at the moment. The map is made with [b]3000 individual hexes[/b]. The feature of this scenario is the [b]most intensive ground battles[/b] in the whole game. Also, both sides of the battle will have [b]a large number of armored vehicles[/b].

notes.title: Moscow was one of the primary military and political objectives for Axis forces
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/BHgOQEv.jpg[/img]
The Battle of Moscow was a military campaign that took place between October 1941 and January 1942.

German offensive towards the Soviet capital was nothing less than an "all-out attack". Moscow was one of the primary military and political objectives for Axis forces in their invasion of the Soviet Union.

The German strategic offensive, named Operation Typhoon, called for two pincer offensive. Initially, the Soviet forces conducted a strategic defense by constructing three defensive belts. 

As the German offensives were halted, a Soviet strategic counter-offensive and smaller-scale offensive operations forced the German armies back.

It was a major setback for the Germans, the end of the idea of a fast German victory in the USSR.

We reproduced the tension of those days. Such small details as the Kremlin on the map do matter too. Water - in progress :)

notes.title: Battle of Stalingrad
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/bFy8Ajl.jpg[/img]
We could not skip the battle that is often regarded as the [b]single largest and bloodiest battle in the history[/b] of warfare.

[b]The Battle of Stalingrad[/b] in 1942 was the most major confrontation of WWII. Germany fought the Soviet Union for control of the city of Stalingrad.

The battle was marked by fierce close quarters combat and direct assaults on civilians in air raids. It lasted five months and the result was almost 2 million killed, wounded or captured on both sides. It was an extremely costly defeat for German forces.

[b]Scenario features[/b]:
- close quarters combat;
- Soviet plants supplying ammo and vehicles;
- a lot of snipers in the Soviet army including [b]Vasily Zaytsev[/b].

notes.title: #8 scenario: Siege of Tobruk
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/B3fSRXP.jpg[/img]
This is one of my favorite scenarios! [b]Sea, sands and palm trees like in pirate stories :)[/b]

The siege lasted for 241 days in 1941 after Axis forces advanced in Operation Sonnenblume against Allied forces in Libya. 

The port was attacked by a force under Erwin Rommel and continued during three relief attempts. The occupation of Tobruk deprived the Axis of a supply port closer to the Egypt–Libya border, which was within the range of Royal Airforce bombers.

The siege diverted Axis troops from the frontier and the Tobruk garrison repulsed several Axis attacks. The port was frequently bombarded by artillery, dive-bombers and medium bombers, as the RAF flew defensive sorties from airfields far away in Egypt. 

Allied naval forces ran the blockade, carrying reinforcements and supplies in and wounded and prisoners out. On 27 November, Tobruk was relieved by the Eighth Army in Operation Crusader.

notes.title: Another scenario: Battle of France
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/I4Py3Sa.jpg[/img]
It is the German invasion of France and the Low Countries during the WWII. 

We use heavy tank Char B1bis on this map. This French heavy tank was a hard target for the Germans. It was a specialized break-through vehicle. Among the most powerfully armed and armored tanks of its day, Char B1bis was very effective in direct confrontations with German armor in 1940.

Still in 1940 German forces defeated Allied forces by mobile operations and conquered France, Belgium, Luxembourg and the Netherlands in six weeks.

Fall Rot was the second phase of the conquest of France. The remaining French divisions made a determined resistance but were unable to overcome the German air superiority and armored mobility. 

I guess mobility is the keystone in a fight with Char B1bis :)

notes.title: Battle of Dunkirk will be the fifth scenario in Panzer Strategy
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/BZli3ri.jpg[/img]

The Battle of Dunkirk took place in France. As part of the Battle of France on the Western Front, the Battle of Dunkirk was the defense and evacuation to Britain of British and other Allied forces in Europe from 26 May to 4 June 1940.

The German army was to halt for three days, which gave the Allies sufficient time to organize the Dunkirk evacuation and build a defensive line.

The War Office made the decision to evacuate British forces on 25 May. In the nine days, 338,226 men escaped aboard 861 vessels (243 were sunk during the operation).

We will try to reproduce conditions of this dramatic battle in our scenario.

notes.title: Two questions about the ship systems
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/7xDuR99.jpg[/img]
[i]Q: How to choose a weapon from the various ship armament?[/i]

Just [b]click on a weapon icon[/b] on the right interface column. If you don't do it, a weapon will be picked automatically.

[i]Q: How an enemy deals damage to the ship's systems?[/i]

When an enemy attacks a ship, points of damage [b]will share randomly[/b] among its systems.

Every system has its own STR. Armored systems (such as the Main Battery) lose 1 STR per 1 point of damage. 

Light or unarmored systems (such as the torpedo tubes or anti-air guns) lose 2 STR per 1 point of damage.

notes.content: Check Your Six! vs Panzer Strategy. In the ‘Battle of the Wargames Wot Have Hit Steam in the Past Week and Feature Hexagons and WW2 and Suchlike’ there can be only one, two, or zero winners. If you’re happy to adopt the role of Reader for the next five minutes, I’ll don the mantle of Critic and, using screenshots and conglomerations of letters arranged in sequence and separated with punctuation marks and spaces of varying lengths, liberally dust you with my novichok-strength opinions. notes.title: Destroyer vs Battleship
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/b57bbvx.jpg[/img]
The [b]battleship[/b] has the most powerful artillery aboard. It is capable to destroy several smaller ships. 

The [b]destroyer[/b] has quick-firing guns only, but it allows to protect battleships against air attacks. Also, destroyers have sonars which make them ideal for hunting submarines.

[b]Destroyers are anti-battleship units[/b]. If a quick destroyer moves close enough (2 hexagons) to a battleship it will attack with torpedos.

notes.title: Railway stations in Panzer Strategy
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/mLYFAhV.jpg[/img]
While the Early Access version of the game is being reviewed by Valve I will say some words about the [b]Railway stations[/b] in the game :) 

Railway stations allow [b]transferring troops and cargos over long distances[/b]. That's why they're often positioned near Sea Ports or Supply Depots.

Cargos are delivered to a station by а railroad, then transferred by trucks to [b]the nearest Supply Depot[/b].

So if Supply Depots are near railway stations connected by a railroad, cargos [b]will be transferred between depots in one turn[/b] without regard to distance. 

If the enemy controls the railroad between stations, [b]the supply will be broken[/b].

We have added [b]animation showing[/b] the connection between railway stations and depots. This animation helps to choose the right target to break the enemy's supply system.

notes.title: System of attachements
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/86ynvTM.jpg[/img]

The system of "attachements" makes the gameplay of Panzer Strategy [b]really flex­ible[/b].

For instance any mac­hine gun "attached" to an infantry unit giv­es it additional pro­tection from air att­acks. Any machine gun has Anti-aircraft effect, moreover different machine guns have different effects. So an infantry unit can receive Anti­-aircraft skills! 

[b]Attachments can change the tactical role greatly[/b]. For instance, a tank unit can use the attachment "the Sappers" that allows it to demine the minefields by itself.

Moreover a player wi­ll be able to attach a Hero to some units to make his own sets of unique skill­s. [b]So these elements make you feel really in charge of your army[/b].

notes.title: Supply system
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/xu2Uhx9.jpg[/img]
A unit has its own reserve of ammo, fuel and so on. It must replenish it though. 

The supply is [b]literally a vehicle with ammo and fuel that is passing[/b] from the unit to a supply depot. If this truck is destroyed the unit will not receive any ammo and won't have the possibility to attack. 

Moreover supplying depots are joined to the net by roads. If a road is cut by the enemy certain depots' reserves will end and the units will not receive ammo and fuel. Their efficiency will drop to zero. 

[b]So supply lines are extremely important in Panzer Strategy as well as maneuvering[/b].

Build your supply system, maneuver to cut the enemy supply lines in order to exhaust him and destroy!

Luftwaffe attacks British transport vessels. In the nine days from 27 May–4 June 243 vessels were sunk, but more than 330 000 men escaped. Luftwaffe lost about 135 aircrafts.
